description:
Fetch one dashboard widget (a chart, tile or list the Plutus app shows) for a source, window and setting you choose, so the user sees the same picture the app draws. `widget_id` is a `catalog_id` from list_dashboard_widget_catalog, which says each widget's `shape`, the `report_scopes` it can speak for, its `window_mode` and the schema of its `data` (ask for it with `data_schema_for`). Pick by what the user wants to see: spend over time `spend-trend` (config `dimension`, `top` 2-7, `chart` "stacked-bar" or "line"); a ranked split `spend-breakdown` (`dimension`, `top`); usage over time `usage-trend` (scope `usage_source`, config `metric`); events on the timeline `event-lanes` or `event-volume` (scope `event_source`); which events were followed by a cost move `event-impact`; budgets, anomalies, commitments and the rest from the catalog. To see two things together, call this once per widget.

`scope_type` is "account" (default), "cost_source", "event_source", "usage_source" (then `scope_ref` is one source id or a comma-separated list) or "tag" (`scope_ref` is the tag value and `tag_key` is required); a widget refuses a scope it does not serve and says so in `unavailable`. `start_date` and `end_date` are YYYY-MM-DD, end exclusive, default the last 30 days (event-impact 61), at most 400 days. Money is in `currency` (default USD). An envelope with `unavailable` set carries a reason and no data: say what it says, not that there was no spend. `truncated` means a list was cut; say so. The widget names no cause for a change: do not add one.

In apps that show MCP Apps (Claude on the web, desktop and mobile), the widget is drawn under the tool call as the app's own chart, so the user already sees it. Say in a sentence or two what it shows and what stands out; do not restate its data as a table or draw another chart of it unless the user asks for one.

scope_ref.description: A source id or comma-separated list, or a tag value

name: get_widget
